name: license-guardian-mcp

tools.name: audit_package_json
tools.description: Audit the LICENSES of every dependency declared in a package.json BEFORE you install or ship. Resolves each dependency's REAL license from the live npm registry (licenses change between versions — packages relicense to AGPL/BUSL/SSPL) and flags copyleft (GPL/LGPL/MPL), network-copyleft (AGPL/SSPL — the SaaS trap), source-available (BUSL/Elastic — looks open, isn't), non-commercial, and missing/unlicensed dependencies that are incompatible with your project's license. Returns a CLEAN / REVIEW / BLOCK verdict per dependency with the exact legal obligation. The free tier audits up to 5 shipping dependencies locally; a LARGER tree (or pro=true) runs unlimited server-side behind payment. ALWAYS run this when an AI agent adds dependencies to a project that will be shipped commercially or as a closed SaaS.

package_json.description: The full package.json content (as a string).

context.description: Your project's distribution context, which decides what is compatible: 'proprietary' (you ship closed-source software — default), 'saas-backend' (closed backend served over a network — flags AGPL/SSPL network-copyleft traps), 'permissive' (your project is MIT/Apache and you want to stay non-copyleft), or 'copyleft-ok' (your project is itself GPL/AGPL).

include_dev.description: Also audit devDependencies (default false — dev deps usually don't ship).

pro.description: When true, run the UNLIMITED pro audit server-side (no 5-dependency free cap, no rate limit). Requires an API key (set LICENSE_GUARDIAN_KEY in your MCP env); without one you'll get instructions to unlock it. The free small-input audit needs no key and runs locally.

tools.name: audit_dependencies
tools.description: Audit the licenses of an explicit list of npm packages (e.g. the deps an AI just chose to add). Accepts 'name' or 'name@version'. Same compatibility engine as audit_package_json: flags copyleft / network-copyleft / source-available / non-commercial / unlicensed packages for your project context. The free tier audits up to 5 packages locally; a longer list (or pro=true) runs unlimited server-side behind payment. Use before running the install command for a set of suggested packages.

context.description: Your project's distribution context, which decides what is compatible: 'proprietary' (you ship closed-source software — default), 'saas-backend' (closed backend served over a network — flags AGPL/SSPL network-copyleft traps), 'permissive' (your project is MIT/Apache and you want to stay non-copyleft), or 'copyleft-ok' (your project is itself GPL/AGPL).

tools.name: explain_license
tools.description: Resolve and explain the REAL license of a single npm package (optionally a specific version, e.g. 'next@13.0.0'). Returns the SPDX id, plain-language obligations, copyleft strength, OSI status and commercial risk — the facts an agent should never guess, because they change per version. Always free. Use before adding any dependency you are unsure about.

name.description: Package name or name@version, e.g. 'lodash' or 'mongodb@5.0.0'.
